source.note: Gap filled (plan row 142 had no source). Twin-jet airliner by weirdybeardyman on OpenGameArt, CC0 per the page; the gear-up .blend (opened with auto-run off), for sky shots. Chosen over the other CC0 candidates rendered side by side (alpaqagames' Low poly cartoon plane, weirdybeardyman's Toy Plane; NuclearOsmosis' Jumbo Jet wide body exports a mesh without a material) because an airliner silhouette is the most useful in anime sky shots and this one is cleanly modelled: swept wings with winglets, two underwing turbofans, a conventional low tailplane. The page's fake-airline livery textures are not inside the .blend, so it ingests untextured, which suits the cel look: a pale body that reads against sky. Real size: a narrow-body twin-jet (737/A320 class, about 38 m long, 12 m tall); rest height 11 m to the fin tip gives 39.1 m long and 30.5 m across the wings. The lowest point is the engine nacelles, at y = 0 (gear up: it belongs in the sky). The tailplanes are one-sided plates, so the body is drawn double-sided (otherwise their ink hull showed black from above). One rigid body, no propeller; static, no clips.
